https://github.com/foxthefox/ioBroker.ecoflow-mqtt — lib/dict_data/ef_powerkit_data.js (bp1/bp2/bp3 verified identical at 61 keys each; kitscc, ldac, lddc, ichigh, iclow, bbcin, bbcout, bmsTotal field lists)

transport: Same EcoFlow cloud REST + MQTT, with one structural difference: a Power Kit is a parent serial number with child modules underneath. Writes carry moduleType and moduleSn to address a specific module (moduleType values 15362 and 15365 appear in tolwi's payloads) rather than addressing the kit as a whole.
blocks: Per-module JSON namespaces: kitscc (MPPT solar charge controller — pv1InVol/pv1InCurr/pv1InWatts, pv2*, batVol/batCurr/batWatts, chgEnergy/dsgEnergy/dayEnergy, hs1Temp/hs2Temp/pcbTemp, mppt1SwSta/mppt2SwSta), iclow and ichigh (inverter-chargers), ldac (AC distribution, acChWatt[0..5], acChCur[0..5], acChSta), lddc (DC distribution, dcChCur[0..11], dcChRelay.1..6), bbcin and bbcout (DC-DC converters, alternator charging), bp1/bp2/bp3 (battery packs), bmsTotal, wireless, onLineModuleSnList.
refutedOnReview: Sources verified as real and largely accurate, but the claim's model list is unsupported.  VERIFIED (I cloned tolwi and evaluated ef_powerkit_data.js in a VM): - devices/public/powerkit.py exists, 764 lines. Module names bbcin, bbcout, ichigh, iclow, kitscc, ldac, lddc all present as device_type branches; packs matched by device_type.startswith("bp"). moduleSn/moduleType addressing (types 15362 and 15365) at lines 11
gotchas: Cloud-only, same as every other EcoFlow dialect here. A Power Kit is a permanent installation in a cabin or RV, so 'needs EcoFlow's servers to be reachable to read your own battery' is a harder constraint here than on a portable unit.
Addressing is two-level. Every write needs moduleType and moduleSn; a driver that models a Power Kit as one device with one address will not be able to write anything.
The kWh figures in the retail listings are pack configurations, not distinct products. Do not research them as four models.
The retail listing claims Bluetooth, WiFi and EcoFlow app. The WiFi is the hub's outbound uplink to EcoFlow, not a LAN server.

ioBroker has powerkitbp2000 and powerkitbp5000 entries, but they are stubs of under 200 characters containing a single key — they do not constitute per-pack-type maps and should not be read as evidence of one.
unmappedReports: dcChCur[0..11] and acChWatt[0..5] / acChCur[0..5] — per-circuit current and power in the DC and AC distribution modules. This is a metered breaker panel and it is the most useful thing a Power Kit reports, and MetricKind has no indexed per-circuit metric at all. A driver would have to mint twelve devices or twelve metric names., dcChRelay.1..6 — per-circuit relay control. switch-state and set-switch fit a single relay; six of them on one module do not, for the same indexing reason., chgEnergy / dsgEnergy on the solar charge controller and dayEnergy on several modules — cumulative energy in and out per module. ac-energy-today and pv-energy-today are close but are not per-module and not bidirectional., busVol — the DC bus voltage tying the modules together, distinct from any single pack voltage., altCableLen / altCableUnit and alt1VoltLmt / alt2VoltLmt on kitscc — alternator cable length and voltage limits, used to derate alternator charging. No MetricKind, no CommandKind., pv1ErrCode / pv2ErrCode / eventCode1 / eventCode2 / warnCode1 / warnCode2 — module fault and warning codes., passByModeEn, passByCurrMax, pfcDsgModeEn, dsgLowPwrEn — shore-power pass-through and discharge behaviour modes., onLineModuleSnList — which modules are currently present. There is no notion in the contract of a device whose sub-device list changes at runtime., DeviceKind gap, differently shaped from the portable stations: a Power Kit is a solar-charger, an inverter, a charger, a battery and a metered distribution panel. There is no DeviceKind for a distribution panel or breaker box at all, which is the piece with no home.
